title: Neuctra UI: SEO, AEO and GEO Guide
intro: A practical playbook for making sites built with @neuctra/ui rank in search engines (SEO), get picked as the answer in featured snippets, AI Overviews and voice (AEO), and get cited by generative engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini (GEO). It includes page templates for tool, category and home pages, site-wide essentials, and ads readiness. Pair it with the generate_page_seo tool (per-page meta, OpenGraph and a woven JSON-LD graph for your framework) and the audit_page_seo tool (pass/warn/fail checks with exact fixes).

topics.title: Technical SEO Foundations
topics.content:
Search engines and AI crawlers can only rank what they can fetch, render and understand.

**Render on the server.** Titles, meta tags, JSON-LD and the main body text must be in the initial HTML (SSR or SSG). Google renders JavaScript late and not always; most AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) do not run JavaScript at all. A client-only SPA that patches `<title>` in a `useEffect` is effectively invisible to them.

**Canonical URLs.** Every indexable page declares one absolute canonical: `<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/docs/button">`. Pick one host (with or without `www`), one protocol (`https`) and one trailing-slash style, and 301-redirect every other variant to it.

**URLs.** Short, lowercase, kebab-case, readable: `/docs/date-picker`, not `/Docs/DatePicker?id=12`. Never change a live URL without a 301 redirect.

**robots.txt.** Lives at `/robots.txt`, points to the sitemap, and blocks only what must never be crawled (admin, API, internal search results):

```text
User-agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin/

Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
```

`robots.txt` controls crawling, not indexing. To keep a crawlable page out of results use `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` (and do not also block it in robots.txt, or the noindex is never seen).

**XML sitemap.** Lists every canonical, indexable URL (never redirects, 404s or noindex pages) with an accurate `<lastmod>`. Regenerate it on every build (e.g. `next-sitemap`, `@astrojs/sitemap`) and submit it in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

**Site architecture.** Every important page is reachable within 3 clicks of the home page and has at least one internal link pointing to it (no orphan pages). Use real `<a href>` links; buttons with `onClick` navigation are not crawled.

**Status codes.** 200 for real pages, 301 for permanent moves, 404/410 for removed pages. A "not found" screen that returns 200 (soft 404) wastes crawl budget.

**noindex** thin or utility pages: login, cart, account, internal search, tag pages with one post, paginated archives beyond page 1 if they add nothing.

**International sites.** Use `hreflang` alternates (`<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de" href="...">`) plus `x-default`, and keep one language per URL.

**HTTPS and security.** HTTPS everywhere, no mixed content, HSTS enabled.

**Only the widget may be client-only.** Interactive tools (editors, converters, canvas, file processing) often need `dynamic(() => import("./Tool"), { ssr: false })` or a client-only island. Wrap only the widget that way. The page frame around it (breadcrumb, H1, lead paragraph, article sections, FAQ and JSON-LD) must render on the server. If the whole page is client-only, the built HTML has no H1, no text and no schema, and crawlers see an empty page.

**One URL registry.** Keep every route in one data file (e.g. `lib/routes.js` with categories and pages, each with an `href`). Generate navigation, the sitemap, `llms.txt`, breadcrumbs and related links from it, so a renamed URL can't leave stale links behind.

**Redirect old slugs.** When a URL changes, add a permanent 301 from the old path, update the registry, and regenerate the sitemap and `llms.txt`. They must list only final URLs, never URLs that redirect.

**Sitemap dates.** Set `<lastmod>` to the date the content really changed, not the build time for every URL: a lastmod that always changes is ignored. Google ignores `<priority>` and `<changefreq>`, so don't spend effort tuning them. Exclude admin, API, 404 and other noindex routes.

topics.title: Performance and Core Web Vitals
topics.content: Core Web Vitals are a ranking signal and a conversion factor. Targets at the 75th percentile of real users: ```text LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) < 2.5s INP (Interaction to Next Paint) < 200ms CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) < 0.1 ``` **LCP** * The hero image is the usual LCP element: serve it in AVIF/WebP, sized to the viewport, and mark it high priority (`priority` on `next/image`, `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"` on a plain ``). * Lazy-load everything below the fold. * Preconnect to critical third-party origins; self-host fonts where possible. **CLS** * Give every image, video and embed explicit `width`/`height` or an `aspect-*` class. * Reserve space for banners, ads and late-loading content. * Load fonts with `font-display: swap` and a size-matched fallback. **INP** * Keep main-thread tasks under 50ms: split large bundles, defer non-critical scripts, avoid heavy work in click handlers. * Load analytics and chat widgets after interaction or idle. **Measure** with PageSpeed Insights (field + lab data), the Search Console Core Web Vitals report and Lighthouse. Lab scores alone are not what Google ranks on. **Avoid layout shift from theme and ads** * Apply the saved light/dark theme with a tiny inline script in `` before first paint, so the page doesn't flash and re-layout. * Reserve the height of ad slots and embeds before they load, and only load them when they near the viewport.

topics.title: On-Page SEO
topics.content:
**Title tag** (the single strongest on-page signal)
* 50 to 60 characters (Google truncates around 580px).
* Primary keyword first, then a benefit or differentiator, then the brand: `React Date Picker Component: Accessible and Themeable | Neuctra UI`, `Merge PDF Online Free: Combine Files, No Sign-Up | Brand`.
* Long-tail modifiers people actually search belong in the title when true: "free", "online", "no sign-up", "without watermark", "for React".
* **One brand-suffix rule for the whole site.** Add ` | Brand` in exactly one place (a title template or one metadata builder) and never hand-type it into individual titles. Mixing the two produces missing suffixes on some pages and doubled ones (`| Brand | Brand`) on others.
* Unique on every page. Never "Home", "Untitled" or the same title site-wide.
* Home page: `Brand: what it is in plain words`.

**Meta description** (not a ranking factor, but it drives click-through)
* 140 to 155 characters.
* Formula: primary keyword + what the page or tool does + trust points + call to action. Example: "Merge PDF files online for free. Combine documents in seconds, right in your browser. No upload, no sign-up, no watermark. Merge your PDFs now."
* Trust points that are true for the page ("no sign-up", "files never leave your device", "free forever") lift click-through.
* Unique per page. If missing or weak, Google writes its own from page text.

**Headings**
* Exactly one `<h1>`, matching the search intent and close to the title (not identical is fine).
* `<h2>`/`<h3>` in order, never skipping levels. Phrase several `<h2>`s as the questions people actually search.

**Body**
* Primary keyword (or a close variant) in the first 100 words.
* Cover the topic completely: answer the main question, the follow-up questions and the obvious objections.
* Short paragraphs, lists and tables where they fit. Write for people; no keyword stuffing.

**Links**
* Descriptive internal anchor text ("React table component", never "click here").
* Link down to child pages and across to related pages. Link out to authoritative sources when you cite facts.

**Images**
* Descriptive `alt` text for meaningful images, empty `alt=""` for decorative ones.
* Descriptive file names (`react-date-picker-dark-mode.webp`).

**Social previews**
* OpenGraph and Twitter tags with a 1200x630 image on every shareable page.

**Social copy.** OpenGraph title and description may be a shorter, punchier variant of the SEO title and description (`og:title` does not need the brand suffix). Every page still needs its own `og:image`.

**Meta keywords.** Google ignores `<meta name="keywords">`. Research long-tail variants (free, online, no sign-up, without watermark, for beginners, vs competitor) and use them in the title, H2s, body and FAQ questions instead. A keywords tag is harmless, but it does nothing for ranking.

topics.title: Keywords, Search Intent and Site Structure
topics.content:
**One page, one primary intent.** Decide what a page should rank for before writing it:

```text
Informational   "what is a date picker"         guide, docs, blog
Commercial      "best react ui library"          comparison, landing
Transactional   "neuctra ui pricing"             pricing, signup
Navigational    "neuctra ui docs"                home, docs index
```

* Pick one primary keyword and a handful of close variants per page.
* Two pages targeting the same keyword compete with each other (cannibalisation). Merge them or differentiate the intent.

**Topic clusters.** Build a pillar page for each core topic (e.g. "React UI Components") and cluster pages for each subtopic (Button, Modal, Date Picker). The pillar links to every cluster page and every cluster page links back to the pillar and to its siblings. This is how topical authority is earned.

**Research sources.** Google Search Console queries you already rank for on page 2, "People also ask", autocomplete, related searches, competitor pages that rank, and your own support and sales questions.

**Map it.** Keep a simple keyword map (URL, primary keyword, intent, status) so no two pages chase the same query.

topics.title: E-E-A-T and Trust Signals
topics.content:
Google's quality raters look for Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trust. AI engines prefer the same sources when choosing what to cite.

* **Real authorship.** Named authors with a short bio and links to their profiles for articles and guides. Use `author` in the schema.
* **Dates.** Show "Published" and "Last updated" dates on content that ages, and mirror them in `datePublished` / `dateModified`. Only bump `dateModified` when the content really changed.
* **Evidence.** Original data, benchmarks, screenshots, code that runs, and citations to primary sources.
* **Transparency.** About, Contact, Privacy Policy and Terms pages; a physical or company address where relevant.
* **Consistency.** The same brand name, logo and description everywhere (site, GitHub, npm, social profiles, directories).
* **Reputation.** Reviews and mentions on third-party sites count for more than claims on your own site.

topics.title: AEO: Answer Engine Optimisation
topics.content:
AEO targets the answer surfaces: featured snippets, "People also ask", Google AI Overviews, voice assistants. The goal is to be the passage an engine lifts as the answer.

**Answer-first structure**
* Phrase key `<h2>`s as questions: "How do I add a date picker in React?"
* Put a direct, self-contained answer of 40 to 60 words right under the question, then expand with detail.
* Start definitions with the term: "A date picker is a form control that ..."

**Snippet-friendly formats**
* Steps: an ordered list (`<ol>`) with one action per item.
* Comparisons: a real `<table>` with clear column headers.
* Lists of options: an unordered list with the item name first.

**FAQ block on every key page**
* 4 to 8 real questions with concise answers (see the `faq` topic), marked up with `FAQPage` schema.

**Voice and conversational queries**
* Cover long, natural questions ("which react ui library works with tailwind v4").
* Keep answers short and speakable; avoid tables-only answers for questions people ask aloud.

**Make the answer easy to extract**
* Plain HTML text, not text baked into images, canvas or tabs that only render on click.
* One idea per paragraph. No filler introduction before the answer.

topics.title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimisation
topics.content:
GEO targets being retrieved and cited by generative engines: ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and Google AI Mode. They pick sources that are crawlable, clear, specific and trusted.

**1. Let them crawl.** Server-render the content (they rarely run JavaScript) and make an explicit robots.txt decision per bot:

```text
# Search / answer bots: allow these if you want to be cited
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Claude-User
Allow: /

# Training bots: a business decision, allow or disallow
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /
User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /
User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /
```

Blocking a search bot means that engine cannot cite you. Blocking a training bot does not stop citations from its search bot.

**2. Publish llms.txt.** A markdown index at `/llms.txt` (spec: llmstxt.org): an H1 with the site name, a one-paragraph summary in a blockquote, then sections of `- [Page title](url): one-line description`. Optionally `/llms-full.txt` with the full text of key docs. Generate it at build time from the same route registry as the sitemap, so it never lists old URLs that now redirect.

**3. Be the clearest source.**
* State facts plainly and specifically: numbers, versions, dates, limits, prices.
* Keep sections self-contained so a single passage makes sense when quoted alone.
* Add comparison tables, definitions and step lists; engines quote these heavily.
* Cite primary sources and include original data or benchmarks worth citing.

**4. Strengthen the entity.**
* Use the same brand name and one-line description everywhere.
* `Organization` schema with `logo` and `sameAs` links (GitHub, npm, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Wikipedia/Wikidata if you have them).
* Earn mentions on sites the engines already trust: docs aggregators, GitHub, Reddit, Stack Overflow, industry publications, review sites.

**5. Stay fresh.** Show and maintain "Last updated" dates; engines favour current sources for anything version-sensitive.

**6. Get indexed by Bing.** ChatGPT search and Copilot lean on Bing's index: verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools, submit the sitemap and ping IndexNow on publish.

**7. Measure.** Track referral traffic from chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com and copilot.microsoft.com, and regularly ask those engines your target questions to see who they cite.

topics.title: Structured Data and Schema Weaving
topics.content:
Structured data (JSON-LD) tells engines exactly what a page is. **Schema weaving** means emitting one connected `@graph` per page instead of several disconnected blobs, with nodes referencing each other by stable `@id`.

**Stable @id scheme** (reuse the exact same IDs on every page):

```text
Organization    https://example.com/#organization
WebSite         https://example.com/#website
WebPage         https://example.com/docs/card#webpage
BreadcrumbList  https://example.com/docs/card#breadcrumb
Main entity     https://example.com/docs/card#article   (or #product, #software)
FAQPage         https://example.com/docs/card#faq
```

**Every page** gets Organization + WebSite + a WebPage (or subtype) + BreadcrumbList, wired together:
* `WebSite.publisher` -> Organization
* `WebPage.isPartOf` -> WebSite, `WebPage.breadcrumb` -> BreadcrumbList
* main entity `mainEntityOfPage` -> WebPage, `publisher` -> Organization

**Type map**

```text
home       WebPage (+ Organization, WebSite as the main entities)
docs       WebPage + TechArticle
blog       WebPage + BlogPosting (author, datePublished, dateModified, image)
product    WebPage + SoftwareApplication or Product
pricing    WebPage + Product with Offer items (real prices only)
landing    WebPage
faq        FAQPage (as the page type)
about      AboutPage
contact    ContactPage
category   CollectionPage
```

**Example graph**

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@graph": [
    { "@type": "Organization", "@id": "https://example.com/#organization", "name": "Example", "url": "https://example.com", "logo": "https://example.com/logo.png", "sameAs": ["https://github.com/example"] },
    { "@type": "WebSite", "@id": "https://example.com/#website", "url": "https://example.com", "name": "Example", "publisher": { "@id": "https://example.com/#organization" } },
    { "@type": "WebPage", "@id": "https://example.com/docs/card#webpage", "url": "https://example.com/docs/card", "name": "Card Component | Example", "isPartOf": { "@id": "https://example.com/#website" }, "breadcrumb": { "@id": "https://example.com/docs/card#breadcrumb" } },
    { "@type": "BreadcrumbList", "@id": "https://example.com/docs/card#breadcrumb", "itemListElement": [
      { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "Home", "item": "https://example.com/" },
      { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "Docs", "item": "https://example.com/docs" },
      { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "Card", "item": "https://example.com/docs/card" }
    ] },
    { "@type": "TechArticle", "@id": "https://example.com/docs/card#article", "headline": "Card Component", "mainEntityOfPage": { "@id": "https://example.com/docs/card#webpage" }, "publisher": { "@id": "https://example.com/#organization" } }
  ]
}
```

**Rules**
* Structured data must describe what is visible on the page. Never mark up content users cannot see.
* Never invent reviews, ratings, prices or authors. Fake markup risks a manual action.
* Since 2023 Google shows FAQ rich results only for well-known government and health sites, and HowTo rich results are gone. Still add `FAQPage` where there is a visible FAQ: it helps AI Overviews and generative engines understand the Q&A.
* Emit JSON-LD in the server-rendered HTML. Escape `<` as `\u003c` when injecting it into a `<script>` tag.
* Validate every template with Google's Rich Results Test and validator.schema.org before shipping.

Use the `generate_page_seo` tool to build a woven graph for any page.

**One node per type per page.** A page must not emit two `SoftwareApplication`, two `FAQPage` or two `BreadcrumbList` nodes. This happens when a shared page shell emits schema and the individual page adds its own `<script type="application/ld+json">` too. Pick one owner (the shell), pass the data into it, and delete the page-level duplicate.

**One data source for visible content and schema.** Build the visible steps list and the `HowTo` node from the same array, and the visible FAQ accordion and the `FAQPage` node from the same array. They then can't drift apart, and nothing is shown twice.

**Tool and web-app pages** (free online tools, converters, calculators, generators):
* `SoftwareApplication` with `applicationCategory` (e.g. `UtilitiesApplication`, `DeveloperApplication`, `MultimediaApplication`), `operatingSystem` ("Web" or "All"), `featureList`, `isAccessibleForFree: true` and an `Offer` with `price: "0"` only if the tool really is free.
* `HowTo` with the visible usage steps. Google no longer shows HowTo rich results, but engines still use the steps for answers.
* `BreadcrumbList` (Home > Category > Tool) and `FAQPage`.

**Listing pages**
* Category or collection pages: `CollectionPage` + an `ItemList` of the pages it links to, in visible order.
* Home page: `ItemList`s for the main categories and popular items, next to Organization and WebSite.

**Optional extras, with honest expectations**
* `WebSite` `potentialAction` `SearchAction`: fine if the site has search, but Google retired the sitelinks search box in 2024, so it no longer changes how results look.
* `speakable`: a beta mostly limited to news publishers; low value for other sites.

topics.title: Writing FAQs That Rank and Get Cited
topics.content:
**Where the questions come from:** Google "People also ask", autocomplete, Search Console queries, Reddit and forum threads, support tickets and sales calls. Never invent questions nobody asks.

**Per page**
* 4 to 8 questions, specific to that page. Never reuse the same FAQ block across pages.
* Question as the user would type or say it: "Does the date picker support keyboard navigation?"
* Answer in 40 to 80 words: direct answer in the first sentence, then the key detail. Plain text, no marketing fluff.
* Include the page's primary keyword or entity name naturally in at least one question.

**Markup**
* Render the FAQ visibly on the page (an Accordion is fine, as long as the text is in the HTML).
* Mirror the exact same questions and answers in `FAQPage` schema (`mainEntity` of `Question` items with an `acceptedAnswer` `Answer`).
* The visible text and the schema text must match word for word.

**Maintenance**
* Update answers when the product changes, and bump `dateModified`.
* Add new questions as support and search data reveal them.

topics.title: Per-Page Meta Checklist
topics.content:
Every indexable page ships these tags in the server-rendered `<head>`:

```html
<html lang="en">
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Primary Keyword: Qualifier | Brand</title>
<meta name="description" content="140 to 155 characters, unique, with the value and a reason to click.">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/path">
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow, max-image-preview:large">

<meta property="og:type" content="website">          <!-- "article" for blog posts -->
<meta property="og:site_name" content="Brand">
<meta property="og:title" content="Same as or close to the title">
<meta property="og:description" content="Same as or close to the description">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/path">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og/path.png">   <!-- 1200x630 -->
<meta property="og:image:alt" content="What the image shows">

<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
<meta name="twitter:title" content="...">
<meta name="twitter:description" content="...">
<meta name="twitter:image" content="https://example.com/og/path.png">

<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#ffffff">

<script type="application/ld+json">{ "@context": "https://schema.org", "@graph": [ ... ] }</script>
```

Checks:
* Title and description are unique across the whole site.
* Canonical and `og:url` are absolute and identical.
* OG image URL is absolute, 1200x630, under about 5MB, and readable at small sizes.
* Blog posts also get `article:published_time` and `article:modified_time`.
* Utility pages use `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">`.

topics.title: Where Metadata Goes in Each Framework
topics.content:
Neuctra UI runs anywhere React 18+ and Tailwind v4 run. The rule is the same everywhere: metadata and JSON-LD must be in the server-rendered HTML. The `generate_page_seo` tool outputs a ready snippet for each of these.

**Next.js App Router** (`framework: "nextjs-app"`)
* `export const metadata = {...}` or `export async function generateMetadata()` in `page.js` or `layout.js`. Use `alternates.canonical`, `openGraph`, `twitter`, `robots`.
* Set `metadataBase: new URL("https://example.com")` in the root layout so relative URLs resolve.
* A `"use client"` page cannot export metadata: put it in the route's `layout.js` instead.
* **Metadata merging is shallow.** A child segment's `openGraph` object replaces the parent's completely. If a page sets `openGraph` at all, it must repeat `images` (and `siteName`, `locale`), or the page ships without an `og:image`. The same applies to `twitter`.
* **Title template.** `title: { template: "%s | Brand", default: "..." }` in the root layout adds the suffix to child titles. Child titles must then not include the brand themselves, or it doubles. When a builder already returns a full title, use `title: { absolute: "..." }` so the template is skipped.
* **Robots for Googlebot** uses kebab-case keys: `robots: { index: true, follow: true, googleBot: { index: true, follow: true, "max-image-preview": "large", "max-snippet": -1, "max-video-preview": -1 } }`. camelCase keys like `maxImagePreview` are ignored.
* **Client-only widgets:** `dynamic(() => import("./Widget"), { ssr: false })` must wrap only the widget. Keep the H1, text, FAQ and JSON-LD in the server-rendered `page.js`.
* `output: "export"` (static export) is fully crawlable: everything above still applies, and you can check the result in the `out/` HTML.
* JSON-LD: render `<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(jsonLd).replace(/</g, "\\u003c") }} />` in the page or layout.
* `app/sitemap.js` and `app/robots.js` generate those files natively.

**Next.js Pages Router** (`"nextjs-pages"`)
* `import Head from "next/head"` and render the tags inside `<Head>`. Pages are pre-rendered, so crawlers see them.

**Vite + React SPA** (`"react-vite"`)
* React 19 hoists `<title>`, `<meta>` and `<link>` rendered anywhere in the tree into `<head>`. On React 18 use `react-helmet-async`.
* Warning: a client-only SPA ships an empty HTML shell. Prerender the routes at build time or move to an SSR framework (Next.js, React Router, Astro, TanStack Start) for anything that must rank or be cited.

**React Router v7 / Remix** (`"react-router"`)
* Export `meta()` from the route module returning `[{ title }, { name: "description", content }, { tagName: "link", rel: "canonical", href }, { "script:ld+json": jsonLd }]`.

**Astro** (`"astro"`)
* Put the tags in the layout's `<head>`, passing title/description as props. JSON-LD: `<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(jsonLd)} />`. Use React islands for Neuctra UI components. `@astrojs/sitemap` builds the sitemap.

**TanStack Start** (`"tanstack-start"`)
* Return `{ meta, links, scripts }` from the route's `head()` option; JSON-LD goes in `scripts` as `{ type: "application/ld+json", children: JSON.stringify(jsonLd) }`.

**Gatsby** (`"gatsby"`)
* `export const Head = () => (<>...tags...</>)` from the page component.

**Plain HTML / other** (`"html"`)
* Put the tags from the `meta-checklist` topic directly in `<head>`.

topics.title: Page Templates for Tool, Category and Home Pages
topics.content:
Consistent templates make every page crawlable, answerable and internally linked by default.

**Tool / product page** (e.g. a free online tool or a single feature):

```text
<main>
  <header>
    Visible breadcrumb      Home > Category > Tool (matches BreadcrumbList)
    Category Badge
    H1                      primary keyword + differentiator
    Lead paragraph          text-secondary, 1 to 2 sentences, keyword in it
  </header>
  The tool / product UI     client-only widget is fine here
  <article>
    <section> H2 intro      what it is, who it's for, keyword in first 100 words
    <section> H2 "How to <task>"   <ol> steps (same data as the HowTo schema)
    <section> H2 benefits    H3 per benefit
    <section> H2 "Who uses <tool>"  use cases + 3 to 4 related links
    <section> H2 privacy / trust    e.g. "Your files stay on your device"
    <section> H2 FAQ         accordion, 6 to 8 questions (same data as FAQPage)
  </article>
</main>
```

**Category page**
* H1 + lead paragraph, then an H2 above the grid of items (never jump from H1 to H3 card titles).
* Each card links to its page with descriptive anchor text.
* `CollectionPage` + `ItemList` + `BreadcrumbList` schema.

**Home page**
* H1 stating what the site is, a lead paragraph, the main categories and popular items, a short FAQ.
* `Organization`, `WebSite`, `ItemList`s of categories and popular items, `FAQPage`.

**Internal linking**
* Render related links from the route registry with a shared `RelatedLinks` component and the framework's link component (`next/link`, `<Link>`), never hand-typed `<a>` tags that go stale.
* Link each page to its category, 3 to 4 siblings, and the category to every child.

topics.title: Site-Wide Essentials
topics.content:
Set these once in the root layout and every page inherits them.

* `<html lang="...">`, `<meta name="viewport">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`.
* A default `og:image` (1200x630), overridden per page or per category where you can.
* `Organization` with `logo` and `sameAs` (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, ...) and `WebSite` with `publisher`, both with stable `@id`s.
* Search engine verification: `google-site-verification` and `msvalidate.01` meta tags (or DNS verification).
* `manifest.webmanifest`, `theme-color`, favicon (SVG + ICO) and `apple-touch-icon` (180x180).
* Privacy-friendly analytics that separates organic and AI-referral traffic.
* Fonts with `font-display: swap`; the theme set before first paint.
* Trust pages linked in the footer: About, Contact (with a real email address), Privacy Policy, Terms, and a Disclaimer where relevant.
* `robots.txt` and the sitemap generated by the build, not maintained by hand.

topics.title: Ads and Monetisation Without Hurting SEO
topics.content:
Ad networks (Google AdSense and others) review trust and content quality, and badly loaded ads hurt Core Web Vitals.

* Publish `/ads.txt` at the site root, generated at build time from your publisher ID.
* Add the network's account verification meta tag in the root layout.
* Load ad scripts after the page is interactive (`strategy="afterInteractive"` or `lazyOnload` with `next/script`), and only when the publisher ID is configured.
* Reserve each slot's size before it loads, and fill slots only when they come near the viewport, to avoid layout shift.
* Never push the main content or the tool below the fold with ads, and never place ads inside the H1/lead block.
* Have About, Contact, Privacy (with the ads and cookie disclosure), Terms and Disclaimer pages live before applying.
* Keep substantial, original content on every monetised page. Thin pages with ads are the most common rejection reason.

topics.title: Off-Page Authority and Monitoring
topics.content:
**Authority**
* Earn links, don't buy them: publish genuinely useful resources (templates, benchmarks, free tools, open-source code), get listed in relevant directories and "awesome" lists, write guest posts and answer questions where your audience asks them.
* Digital PR: original data and strong opinions get cited by journalists and by AI engines.
* Keep the brand consistent across GitHub, npm, social profiles and directories.

**Setup on launch**
* Google Search Console: verify the domain property, submit the sitemap, check indexing and Core Web Vitals reports.
* Bing Webmaster Tools: verify (you can import from Search Console), submit the sitemap, enable IndexNow.
* Analytics that separate organic search and AI referrals (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, copilot.microsoft.com).

**Ongoing**
* Weekly: Search Console coverage errors, new queries on page 2 worth improving.
* Monthly: rankings for target keywords, pages losing clicks, Core Web Vitals, broken links, which sources AI engines cite for your target questions.
* Refresh top pages every few months: new facts, new FAQs, updated `dateModified`.

topics.title: SEO / AEO / GEO Launch Checklist
topics.content:
Run this before any page or site goes live. Every item is pass or fail.

**Check the built HTML, not the source code.** Run the production build and inspect the output (`view-source:`, or grep the static `out/` / `dist/` HTML). Bugs like client-only pages, duplicate schema and missing images only show up there.

**Crawl and index**
- [ ] Content, meta and JSON-LD are in the server-rendered HTML (view source, not DevTools)
- [ ] One absolute canonical per page; all host/protocol/slash variants 301 to it
- [ ] robots.txt allows the site, references the sitemap, has an explicit AI bot policy
- [ ] sitemap.xml lists only canonical 200 pages with accurate lastmod, submitted to Google and Bing
- [ ] Utility and thin pages are noindex; no important page is noindex by mistake
- [ ] No orphan pages; every key page within 3 clicks of home
- [ ] Real 404 status for missing pages
- [ ] Every page has exactly one H1 in the built HTML (a missing H1 usually means the page renders client-only)
- [ ] Sitemap and llms.txt list only final URLs (no 301s), generated from one route registry
- [ ] Sitemap lastmod reflects real content changes

**On-page**
- [ ] Unique title, 50 to 60 characters, keyword first, brand last
- [ ] Unique meta description, 140 to 155 characters
- [ ] Exactly one H1; H2/H3 in order; several H2s phrased as questions
- [ ] Primary keyword in the first 100 words
- [ ] Descriptive alt text on meaningful images
- [ ] OpenGraph + Twitter tags with a 1200x630 image on every page, including category and static pages
- [ ] Brand suffix identical on every title, never missing and never doubled

**Structured data**
- [ ] One woven `@graph`: Organization, WebSite, WebPage, BreadcrumbList + page type node
- [ ] FAQPage only where the FAQ is visible, text identical
- [ ] At most one node of each type per page (no duplicate SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList)
- [ ] Visible steps/FAQs and their schema come from the same data, and nothing is rendered twice
- [ ] No invented reviews, ratings or prices
- [ ] Passes Rich Results Test and validator.schema.org

**AEO / GEO**
- [ ] 40 to 60 word direct answer under each question heading
- [ ] 4 to 8 page-specific FAQs
- [ ] /llms.txt published and generated from the route list
- [ ] Organization `sameAs` links and consistent brand naming
- [ ] Visible "Last updated" date on content that ages

**Performance**
- [ ] LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1 on mobile
- [ ] LCP image high priority, below-fold media lazy, all media sized

Use the `audit_page_seo` tool to check a page against the on-page and schema items automatically.
